articles.title: The seeds of the next recession are being sown in today’s booming economy, warns top economist: ‘Icarus is flying towards the sun’
articles.summary: "Strength comes with growing risks beneath the surface, and the economy increasingly looks like it's in the late stages of the cycle."
articles.body:
While 2026 has been a volatile year for the U.S. economy, headline macroeconomic data tell a relatively healthy story: GDP has grown more than 2% every quarter this year—and a respectable 3.4% in Q3. The unemployment rate is steady at around 4%. And the S&P 500 is up 7% year to date. Admittedly, inflation still looks a little hot, but with the U.S. home to the leaders of the AI revolution, it's easy to be optimistic. What could possibly go wrong? According to Michael Pearce, chief U.S. economist at Oxford Economics, rather a lot. In fact, Pearce believes that the currently strong expansion of the largest economy on earth means the "seeds of the next recession are being sown."

In a note titled "Icarus is flying towards the sun," Pearce suggests the next downturn, when it arrives, will also be "deeper and more painful" as the economy will have less of a fiscal cushion to fall back on, as government money is siphoned off by budget deficits and spiraling interest payments on the national debt.

The case for a recession stems from vulnerabilities in the economy, such as the debt levels used to finance AI spending. Goldman Sachs estimates that $500 billion in AI-related debt has been issued in 2026 thus far, and a further $420 billion will be loaned in 2027.

This presents an obvious snag if, or when, returns are slower to materialize—or don't come to fruition at all.

The second vulnerability Pearce sees is weaker hiring among small businesses, citing Oxford Economics data tracking the share of gross job gains from existing small firms, which has fallen steadily throughout 2026.

Other job market reports tell a more positive story: Payroll expert ADP's latest jobs report shows small businesses (between 1 and 50 employees) added a total of 28,000 jobs in October—more than large employers (500 staff or more), who added only 24,000.

Nevertheless, unemployment has been relatively steady this year despite some months posting weak jobs figures. As such, Pearce notes that signs of a hiring slowdown suggest any layoffs are more likely to feed through into a rising unemployment rate.

The third vulnerability Pearce sees is that the labor market adjustment around AI has "barely begun." Firms tend to restructure staff around downturns rather than periods of expansion. With so many questions still looming for companies, from skills availability to practical application, Pearce suggests this adjustment is unlikely to take place until a downturn happens.

The dot-com bubble holds a warning, he adds: "While the dot-com recession was one of the mildest in terms of GDP, its impact on the labor market was disproportionately severe. The economy continued to shed jobs through summer 2003, and the unemployment rate didn't return to its 2000 nadir until 2018.

articles.title: Barclays, Deutsche Bank See AI Boom Extending Dollar Strength
articles.summary: The dollar is expected to extend its rally into 2027 despite fears of a slowdown in AI spending that could undermine the US currency, according to at least t...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- The dollar is expected to extend its rally into 2027 despite fears of a slowdown in AI spending that could undermine the US currency, according to at least three banks.

Fueled by the artificial intelligence boom, the dollar has climbed as global investors pour into US equities. The greenback has benefited from overseas investors converting local currencies to buy shares of US companies that use the technology. Additionally, the US private sector committing to a four-year AI investment cycle amid a strong US economy with interest rates higher for longer sets a positive backdrop for the greenback, according to Barclays.

"AI capex should remain a growth tailwind in 2027," Barclays Plc strategists led by Themistoklis Fiotakis wrote in a Tuesday note. "We remain bullish on the US dollar."

A gauge of the dollar is up about 3.1% so far this year, strengthening against most of its major peers as a hawkish Federal Reserve and oil prices have also supported the currency.

Deutsche Bank strategists including Tim Baker, George Saravelos and Mallika Sachdeva revised their dollar forecast higher for next year, even after warning earlier this week that growing ties to AI and US equities instead of Treasuries could make the currency more volatile.

"Prospects seem good for the US dollar to remain a high yielder, until and unless the AI boom unwinds," Deutsche Bank strategists wrote in a Wednesday note.

Meanwhile, Barclays brushed off concerns that Democratic control of Congress would derail AI buildout in the near term, noting that existing projects are still set to proceed and hyperscalers show little sign of pulling back.

"The idea is that if the US is innovating at a pace that's increasing productivity growth, increasing earnings, and pushing up equilibrium around interest rates, it makes it very attractive for capital, and that's the biggest driver of the dollar," said Standard Chartered Bank strategist Steven Englander, who expects the dollar to strengthen beyond 2027 as such activity attracts capital into the country.

AI spending could also tilt the outlook for Fed policy toward further tightening, according to Barclays. Traders have ramped up bets on a December rate hike amid a string of hawkish comments from central bank officials.

articles.title: Costco generators sell out as tech outages spark panic buying
articles.summary: From Microsoft to the FAA, a wave of tech outages has rattled Americans, sparking panic buying that sold out most of Costco’s generators online.
articles.body:
A rapid string of high-profile tech outages has rattled Americans and sent them rushing to stock up on emergency supplies.

Retailers like Costco are reaping the benefits of this sudden wave of panic buying. According to Mizuho analyst David Bellinger, shoppers are "pantry loading" and snapping up backup power. As of Oct. 17, 21 of the 26 high-ticket generators Costco offers online were sold out.

"Consumer anxiety following the Microsoft Outlook outage, the ground stoppage for all U.S. airline flights and apocalyptic concerns flaring up across social media have all contributed to increased emergency prep sales," Bellinger wrote in a research note.

Costco did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the sales of generators and other emergency prep supplies from USA TODAY.

The unease stems from a seemingly relentless cascade of system failures. First, Microsoft's ubiquitous office software went dark. Then, the Federal Aviation Administration issued a rare nationwide ground stop. Soon after, a software bug disrupted banking, a United Airlines outage delayed departures and Apple users lost access to iCloud and Apple Pay. As each failure hit, viral posts on TikTok and other platforms urged users to brace for more.

Speaking at a news conference in the Philippines on Nov. 18, Secretary of State Marco Rubio emphasized that there is no evidence the disruptions are connected.

"The Microsoft incident has nothing to do with what we saw with the FAA. The FAA has nothing to do with what we saw with the banks a few days ago. These issues that we've seen from a technical standpoint are completely unrelated one from another," Rubio said.

Even if coincidental, the back-to-back disruptions expose a major vulnerability: America's critical infrastructure relies heavily on concentrated tech systems.

"When one piece fails, it fails at national scale," said Patrick Moorhead, founder of Moor Insights and Strategy.

Because modern systems are so complex and tightly interwoven, a single glitch can instantly snowball and take down essential services, noted University of Notre Dame professor Mike Chapple. And as society grows more dependent on massive-scale tech, experts warn these failures will likely become more frequent and severe.

"Should people panic? No. Should we ask for better engineering? Yes," said Virginia Tech professor Ali Butt. "That means testing changes for their downstream impact, rolling them out in stages, isolating faults and setting clear policies for systems the public depends on."

articles.title: Mais de 13 mil trabalhadores no AP ainda não sacaram o Abono Salarial | G1
articles.standfirst: Prazo para receber o benefício encerra em 28 de dezembro.
articles.summary: Prazo para receber o benefício encerra em 28 de dezembro.
articles.body:
Segundo dados do Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego (MTE), mais de 13 mil trabalhadores ainda não sacaram o abono salarial de 2026 no Amapá. Os dados correspondem a quem trabalhou nos anos de 2019 a 2024. O prazo para receber o dinheiro encerra em 28 de dezembro.

Já foram sacados 99,23% do total de pagamentos previstos para o calendário deste ano. Ao todo, R$ 14,9 milhões ainda estão disponíveis para a retirada.

O valor do benefício varia de R$ 136 a R$ 1.621, conforme o número de meses trabalhados. Podem receber o abono trabalhadores da iniciativa privada e servidores públicos que atendem aos critérios do programa. Em todo o país, mais de 276 mil trabalhadores ainda não sacaram o abono salarial.

O pagamento é feito pela Caixa Econômica Federal, no caso do Programa de Integração Social (PIS), e pelo Banco do Brasil, para quem tem direito ao Programa de Formação do Patrimônio do Servidor Público (Pasep).

Para verificar se tem direito ao benefício, o trabalhador pode consultar o aplicativo Carteira de Trabalho Digital ou o Portal gov.br.

O abono salarial de 2026 é referente ao ano-base 2024. Para receber o benefício, o trabalhador precisa cumprir os seguintes requisitos:

Estar cadastrado no PIS/Pasep há pelo menos cinco anos, contados a partir do primeiro vínculo com empregador contribuinte;

Ter recebido remuneração média mensal de até R$ 2.766 em 2024;

Ter trabalhado por pelo menos 30 dias, consecutivos ou não, durante 2024;

Ter os dados informados corretamente pelo empregador no eSocial.

articles.title: Exoesqueleto: veja aposta chinesa para ajudar na mobilidade de idosos | G1
articles.standfirst: Equipamentos ajudam idosos a caminhar, subir escadas, levantar de cadeiras e até fazer movimentos de fisioterapia. Mercado faz parte da chamada “economia prateada”, que pode movimentar o equivalente a R$ 19 trilhões por ano em 2030.
articles.summary: Equipamentos de alta tecnologia e a economia prateada na China buscam devolver a mobilidade aos idosos com o uso de exoesqueletos e inteligência artificial.
articles.body:
Um exoesqueleto que ajuda a movimentar as pernas e reduz o esforço para caminhar. Um assento inflável que auxilia na hora de levantar da cadeira. Um animal de companhia equipado com inteligência artificial. Banheiros com pisos que secam mais rápido, pias ajustáveis e vasos sanitários acionados por comando de voz.

Na China, o envelhecimento da população está impulsionando o desenvolvimento de tecnologias voltadas a um objetivo comum: permitir que os idosos mantenham a autonomia e a mobilidade por mais tempo.

As soluções fazem parte da chamada “economia prateada”, expressão usada pelo governo chinês para designar o mercado de produtos e serviços destinados à população idosa. A expectativa é que esse setor movimente o equivalente a R$ 19 trilhões por ano em 2030. Para efeito de comparação, o PIB do Brasil em 2025 foi de quase R$ 13 trilhões.

Em Xangai, onde cerca de uma em cada três pessoas é idosa, já existem lojas especializadas nesses produtos.

Uma delas é conhecida como “Loja Prateada de Xangai”, em referência aos cabelos grisalhos de seus clientes. O estabelecimento reúne equipamentos criados para facilitar tarefas cotidianas e permitir que pessoas com limitações físicas dependam menos da ajuda de terceiros.

"Economia Prateada" na China — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Exoesqueleto ajuda a movimentar as pernas

Entre as tecnologias disponíveis está um exoesqueleto preso à cintura e às pernas. Alimentado por uma bateria, o equipamento acompanha os movimentos do usuário e ajuda a levantar as pernas durante a caminhada.

Segundo o fabricante, o aparelho pode diminuir em até 50% o esforço físico.

A tecnologia é usada por um aposentado de Xangai que trabalhou podando árvores nos parques da cidade. Apaixonado por futebol, ele teve problemas nos joelhos desde cedo e, com o passar dos anos, começou a ter dificuldade para caminhar na rua.

Depois de encontrar um anúncio do equipamento em um jornal, pediu ajuda ao filho para comprá-lo.

“Eu tinha dificuldade de andar na rua. Vi um anúncio no jornal e pedi para o meu filho: ‘Compra um desse para mim’.”

Segundo o aposentado, o aparelho faz diferença principalmente ao subir escadas.

“Eu consigo suportar o peso, mas não sinto o peso. Eu sinto que fica mais leve porque a máquina levanta a minha perna. Eu não preciso fazer isso. Para subir escada é melhor ainda.”

Exoesqueleto: veja aposta chinesa para ajudar na mobilidade de idosos — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Para testar o equipamento em condições mais exigentes, o exoesqueleto também foi usado em um percurso de 1.100 degraus até a Grande Muralha da China.

O aparelho ajudou durante a subida, embora não tenha eliminado o esforço provocado pelo trajeto, pelo calor de 32°C e pela alta umidade. Na descida, outra limitação: o sistema deixa de auxiliar os movimentos, e o usuário precisa carregar os cerca de cinco quilos do equipamento.

Subimos a Grande Muralha da China com um exoesqueleto! — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Tecnologia para levantar, caminhar e fazer fisioterapia

O exoesqueleto é apenas uma das soluções destinadas aos idosos.

Na loja especializada de Xangai, há um dispositivo que pode ser colocado sobre uma cadeira. O aparelho infla gradualmente e eleva a pessoa, reduzindo a força necessária para ficar de pé.

Outro equipamento funciona como uma espécie de máquina de fisioterapia. Colocado na mão, faz movimentos de abrir e fechar os dedos de pessoas que perderam parte da capacidade de movimentá-los.

Até uma ida ao mercado pode ganhar adaptações. Um carrinho de compras possui um banco integrado para que o idoso possa parar e descansar quando estiver cansado.

Já quem procura companhia pode encontrar pets equipados com inteligência artificial, capazes de interagir com os usuários.

Chineses investem em tecnologias voltadas à população idosa; veja como funcionam — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Parte dos investimentos também busca tornar as casas mais seguras.

Governos locais oferecem subsídios para a compra de alguns equipamentos, e uma das adaptações mais procuradas é a reforma do banheiro, ambiente onde quedas podem representar um risco maior para idosos.

Entre as soluções disponíveis está um chuveiro que permite o banho sentado e libera uma névoa de água para ajudar a manter a temperatura corporal.

O piso foi desenvolvido para secar mais rapidamente, reduzindo o risco de escorregões. A pia pode subir e descer para se adaptar a pessoas que usam cadeira de rodas, enquanto o vaso sanitário pode ser acionado por controle remoto ou comando de voz.

São tecnologias de diferentes níveis de complexidade, mas pensadas para resolver dificuldades concretas do envelhecimento: levantar, caminhar, tomar banho, carregar compras ou simplesmente ter companhia.

Com uma população cada vez mais velha, a China aposta que esse conjunto de soluções pode representar não apenas um novo mercado, mas também uma maneira de prolongar a independência na velhice.

Uma expressão chinesa citada na reportagem resume essa tentativa de olhar para o envelhecimento sob outra perspectiva: “O vermelho do pôr do sol não é o fim do dia. É quando a luz fica mais bonita.”

A tecnologia, nesse cenário, surge como uma aposta para fazer essa luz durar um pouco mais.

articles.title: Black Friday: por que comprar com desconto dá prazer, mesmo quando gastamos mais? | G1
articles.standfirst: No g1 Explica, a repórter Renata Ribeiro explica e simplifica os temas que dominam o noticiário econômico e mexem diretamente com o nosso bolso.
articles.summary: No g1 Explica, a repórter Renata Ribeiro explica e simplifica os temas que dominam o noticiário econômico e mexem diretamente com o nosso bolso.
articles.body:
Comprar um produto por um preço menor do que o esperado pode aumentar a satisfação do consumidor. O fenômeno é explicado pela “utilidade da transação”, conceito apresentado em 1985 pelo economista Richard Thaler, vencedor do Nobel de Economia em 2017.

Essa sensação de vantagem surge da comparação entre o preço pago e o valor que o consumidor esperava gastar. Na Black Friday, os descontos também podem incentivar a compra de produtos mais caros. Nos EUA, um levantamento da Adobe mostrou que, entre novembro e dezembro de 2025, a participação desses produtos no total de unidades vendidas aumentou 20% em comparação com o restante do ano.

Mas nem todo desconto representa economia. Uma promoção pode levar o consumidor a gastar mais do que planejava. Por isso, antes de comprar, é importante verificar o preço final, consultar o histórico de preços, comparar ofertas e considerar o custo do frete.

articles.title: Megha Engg MD raises $700mn, to buy out founder uncle's stake
articles.summary: Hyderabad: One of India's biggest infrastructure companies is all set to see a change in its ownership pattern.
articles.body: Hyderabad: One of India's biggest infrastructure companies is all set to see a change in its ownership pattern. Megha Engineering and Infrastructures Limited (MEIL) Group's MD, PV Krishna Reddy, has raised about $700 million (Rs 6,600 crore) from a consortium of global investors to buy out the 43% stake held by his uncle and MEIL group founder, P Pitchi Reddy.The transaction, backed by investors including Davidson Kempner, Hillhouse Capital and Varde Partners, has been structured through a mix of structured equity and the proposed monetisation of select road assets. The Hyderabad-based conglomerate, however, refused to give details of the deal.According to sources, the deadline for Krishna Reddy to acquire his uncle's stake as part of the family settlement arrangement was 2027. While earlier Pitchi Reddy held a 51% stake and Krishna Reddy held a 49% stake, Krishna Reddy had increased his stake to 57% over a period of time.Sources said the deal values MEIL at about Rs 1 lakh crore, while its energy transition platform, EPTL, has been valued at around Rs 14,000 crore.A farmer's son from Andhra Pradesh, Pitchi Reddy had started the company in 1989 as a small fabrication and pipe manufacturing workshop in Hyderabad's bustling Balanagar Industrial Estate. Its initial capital was just Rs 5 lakh. Krishna Reddy had joined the operation a couple of years later and played a key role in turning the workshop into an infrastructure giant over the past four decades. MEIL now has operations in more than 20 countries.The group's businesses span irrigation, transport, hydrocarbons, power, manufacturing and clean mobility.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Anthropic raises $81.3bn in biggest IPO of all time
articles.summary: AI giant prices shares at $83 in blockbuster market debut.
articles.body:
Anthropic has raised $81.3bn in the largest initial public offering (IPO) in history, leapfrogging SpaceX’s initial $75bn market debut in June.

The San Francisco-based AI giant said in a statement late on Wednesday that the company and its seven co-founders had sold 980 million shares at $83 each.

The bigger-than-expected IPO comes after investor demand for the stock far outstripped forecasts.

Anthropic had said in corporate filings last week that it intended to offer 825 million shares at between $70 and $78 apiece.

The Claude creator is also set to raise $26bn through a private placement, a type of deal involving the sale of stock to private investors, taking the total capital raised to $107.3bn.

SpaceX’s total IPO haul later came to $85.7bn, after the deal’s underwriters exercised an overallotment option to purchase additional shares.

The blockbuster offering gives Anthropic a market value of roughly $1.5 trillion, making it the world’s 12th-biggest firm at current valuations, just behind Tesla.

Anthropic shares will begin trading on the Nasdaq stock exchange in New York on Thursday under the ticker “ANT”.

The public listing of Anthropic, founded in 2021 by former researchers from rival AI firm OpenAI, has been closely watched as a test of the eye-watering valuations of tech companies leading the AI rollout.

Tech firms have poured trillions of dollars into AI, anticipating it will usher in revolutionary changes in business and society.

AI-related spending is forecast to reach $2.7 trillion in 2026 and $3.6 trillion in 2027, according to technology insights company Gartner.

Companies betting on the frontier technology currently make up roughly half of the value of the S&P 500 index.

The spending frenzy has stoked debate over whether Big Tech is funding a future gold mine or a speculative bubble like the one that preceded the 2000 dot-com crash.

Anthropic’s listing also comes as the market for the advanced graphics processing units that power AI is under a cloud amid the spying claims roiling chip giant Nvidia.

Nvidia co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang stepped down last week amid unproven claims that a woman he was romantically involved with worked with the Chinese intelligence services.

The scandal has fuelled calls in the United States for stronger restrictions on China’s access to high-end chips, casting a pall over an AI boom partly sustained by Chinese developers’ remote access to data centres in Southeast Asia.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite stock index has shed 7.6 percent of its value over the past month, led by a more than 30 percent plunge in Nvidia’s stock price.

Asian stock markets with heavy exposure to AI had a mixed session on Thursday amid the flurry of excitement around Anthropic.

Japan’s benchmark Nikkei 225 rose 0.7 percent, while South Korea’s Kospi closed up 0.9 percent after sliding in morning trading.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index and Taiwan’s Taiex both finished in the red, shedding 2 percent and 4.4 percent, respectively.

Nasdaq futures gained 1.9 percent ahead of Wall Street’s reopening.

Jay R Ritter, an IPO expert at the University of Florida, said that Anthropic’s ability to make profits to justify its valuation will depend on various factors, some of which are outside its control.

“Thirty years ago, the internet was the next big thing. It has changed our lives,” Ritter told Al Jazeera. “Today, artificial intelligence is the next big thing. It will change our lives, too.”

Ritter said investors are particularly excited about the potential of Anthropic’s AI models to find cures for conditions such as cancer and dementia in the near future.

“When Google went public in 2004, no one knew whether it would be able to dominate on-line searches, and no one knew how lucrative the targeted search advertising business would become,” he said.

Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives, said Anthropic’s strong debut should help reassure investors that the AI boom is sustainable.

“At a time in which investors are very nervous on the overall tech trade and the Nvidia black cloud moment casts a shadow over the tech sector, Anthropic’s IPO is a big near-term win for the tech sector and should help restore some investor confidence that the AI revolution growth thesis is not waning,” Ives said in a note to clients.

“It is going through a very turbulent, white-knuckle period that does not change our longer-term view that $3 trillion to $4 trillion of capex will be spent over the next few years on the AI revolution,” Ives said, adding that Anthropic would be “a central player” in the buildout.

articles.title: Nvidia sets record with $65bn Q3 profit
articles.summary: Nvidia Corp sought to deliver a clear message during its first earnings update since the departure of long-time leader Jensen Huang: He's not coming back,
articles.body: Nvidia Corp sought to deliver a clear message during its first earnings update since the departure of long-time leader Jensen Huang: He's not coming back, and the company will be fine without him.Total sales rose 103% to $115.8 billion for the third quarter of fiscal 2027. The champion of semiconductors for artificial intelligence once again exceeded expectations, both in terms of revenue and net income, which reached $65.3 billion.The chip giant boosted its sales forecast for next year and vowed to improve Nvidia's access to critical supplies, while tamping down speculation that Huang might return. The company also added $150 billion to its stock-buyback programme.The shares rose as much as 2.7% to $159.7 on Wednesday after trading got underway in New York. Nvidia's stock has tumbled in recent weeks, battered by the scandal and broader fears that AI spending is poised to slow. It's down about 17% this year."Our supply is growing, our customers and our partners are with us, and employees are committed," interim CEO Colette Kress said during a conference call with analysts Tuesday. "We've got this." It was a high-stakes moment for Kress, who took the reins last week after Huang's ouster - a chaotic exit spurred by multiple extramarital affairs and concerns that he was targeted by a Chinese espionage plot.Nvidia has been the largest beneficiary of the AI build-out, and Huang served as the industry's biggest cheerleader. Now the company looks to ensure that its momentum won't be undermined by the controversy swirling around it."The cards of doubt seemed stacked so high. However, from a bird's-eye view it was a solid 3Q27 print," said Daniel Morgan, a senior portfolio manager at Synovus Trust. articles.summary: Anthropic has emerged with the biggest IPO ever, raising $81.31 billion through its stock-market offering and surpassing SpaceX's $75 billion fundraising.
articles.body: Anthropic has emerged with the biggest IPO ever, raising $81.31 billion through its stock-market offering and surpassing SpaceX's $75 billion fundraising. The artificial intelligence company priced its shares at $83 apiece on Wednesday (local time), above its initially indicated range of $70-$78.The pricing values the San Francisco-based AI company at $1.5 trillion and reflects strong investor demand despite concerns surrounding the technology sector and the possibility of an AI bubble.Anthropic, the maker of the Claude AI tool, is scheduled to begin trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker symbol "ANT". While its initial plan was to offer 825 million shares, the final offering comprises 980 million shares of Class A common stock.Of the total, 956,351,354 shares are being sold by Anthropic itself, while 23,648,646 shares are being offered by certain existing stockholders.The scale of investor interest comes at a time when the market is dealing with several uncertainties. These include the ouster of Nvidia's CEO, concerns about an AI bubble, the possibility of a regulatory crackdown by a Democratic-led Congress next year and growing anti-AI sentiment among the public.Despite these concerns, Anthropic's pricing indicates that investors remain willing to put money into major AI companies.“This is strong appetite for this major AI IPO in Anthropic, and it’s a big win for the tech sector after a white-knuckle time with Nvidia. The pricing shows strong demand among investors,” said Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co.Its rival OpenAI, meanwhile, is not planning to enter the stock market until next year.Heavy spending makes fresh capital importantBeyond setting an IPO record, the fundraising gives Anthropic an opportunity to secure additional capital without adding to its existing debt burden.The company has already borrowed $6.2 billion, an amount it has described as “substantial” in its financial filings. It is also unprofitable under standard accounting rules, suggesting that its resources to service interest and principal payments are limited.Its financial requirements are particularly significant given the scale of its infrastructure commitments. Anthropic has signed leases and other agreements that will require it to spend $900 billion on computing power and infrastructure over the coming years. Of this, $70 billion is due to be spent over the next 12 months.Although the company currently has ample cash, its sizeable spending plans mean those reserves could be used up quickly if it cannot secure additional funding.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Western states drive car sales in Q2, Maharashtra leads
articles.summary: New Delhi: Maharashtra remained India's largest passenger vehicle market in July-Sept.
articles.body: New Delhi: Maharashtra remained India's largest passenger vehicle market in July-Sept. Sales in the state rose about 25% from a year earlier to 1.6 lakh units, while national sales grew 30.7% to 13.6 lakh units, according to the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (Siam). Maharashtra's share of national sales fell from 12.7% to 12.1%.The western region, which includes Maharashtra and Gujarat, retained its lead among Siam's four zones. It sold close to 4.3 lakh passenger vehicles in the second quarter of FY27, up about 25% from year earlier. With sales growing slower than the national market, the region's share slipped from about 33% to 32%.Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat held on to second and third place, accounting for 9.8% and 8.3% of passenger vehicle sales, respectively.Meanwhile, two-wheeler sales rose 15.2% year on year to 64.3 lakh units, the highest for any second quarter. The western region led this segment too, with sales rising about 9% to 21.1 lakh units a year earlier.UP remained the largest two-wheeler market, with sales rising about 14% to close to 7.9 lakh units. articles.title: Employee worked 4 years, 9 months and 12 days, not 5 years, and Bengaluru Metro denied him Rs 1.75 lakh gratuity; Karnataka High Court orders full payment with 10% interest after examining the 240-day rule
articles.summary: Are you entitled to a gratuity payout if you have not completed five years of continuous service with your employer?
articles.body: Are you entitled to a gratuity payout if you have not completed five years of continuous service with your employer? While the Labour codes have undergone a change and some rules have changed, certain pending cases also raise this important question.In one such case, the Karnataka High Court has ruled that an employee who leaves a job before completing five years of continuous service can still qualify for gratuity if the conditions laid down under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, are met.The court held that where an employee has worked for at least 240 days during the 12 calendar months immediately preceding his resignation, the period can be treated as a complete year of service for determining gratuity eligibility.What the case is aboutThe dispute involved a former assistant engineer at Bangalore Metro, whose claim for Rs 1.75 lakh in gratuity was rejected because his tenure fell short of five years.He had worked for four years, nine months and 12 days.The man joined the Bengaluru Metro Rail Corporation (BMRCL) as an assistant engineer on July 6, 2017. He resigned on March 19, 2022, and was formally relieved of his duties on April 18, 2022. His total period of employment amounted to four years, nine months and 12 days.After leaving the corporation, he made several representations seeking payment of gratuity. He claimed Rs 1.85 lakh, calculating the amount on the basis of his last-drawn monthly salary of Rs 64,210.BMRCL declined to release the payment, prompting him to approach the court.Why the court ruled in favour of ex-employeeThe Karnataka High Court observed that the dispute could not be decided simply by checking whether the man had completed five calendar years from the date he joined BMRCL.His entitlement to gratuity had to be assessed by reading Section 4(1) of the Payment of Gratuity Act alongside the definition of “continuous service” provided under Sections 2(c) and 2A.The bench also made it clear that gratuity is not a discretionary payment or a benefit granted by an employer as a matter of goodwill, an ET report said. It is a statutory entitlement that becomes payable when the employee fulfils the conditions prescribed under the law.Section 4(1) of the Payment of Gratuity Act lays down the requirement of five years of continuous service, subject to certain specified exceptions.However, the court said this provision cannot be considered on its own, without taking into account Section 2(c), which defines “continuous service” with reference to Section 2A.Section 2A, in turn, sets out the statutory criteria for determining whether an employee has completed continuous service. Under the circumstances specified in sub-section (2), an employee can be deemed to have completed the prescribed period of continuous service if he has worked for at least 240 days during the relevant 12-calendar-month period.The Karnataka High Court observed that the deeming provision is an integral part of the legal framework for determining continuous service, rather than a factor that can be disregarded.Consequently, an employee’s eligibility cannot be decided merely by counting the calendar time between the date of joining and the end of employment. The actual number of days worked and the applicability of Section 2A of the Payment of Gratuity Act must also be examined.Against this backdrop, the court identified the central issue in the man’s case as whether his employment during the fifth year met the statutory conditions and whether he could claim the benefit of the deeming provision on the basis of the facts placed before the statutory authorities.The Karnataka High Court ruled in favour of the engineer and directed Bangalore Metro to pay him Rs 1.75 lakh along with interest at 10% from May 18, 2022.Explaining the significance of the decision, Mayank Parashar, Legal Associate at Clasis Law-India, told ET: "Karnataka High Court has now re-settled the principle in the context of eligibility of the continuous service requirement for gratuity and concluded that employers should consider the definition of continuous service and key conditions for gratuity together. That’s said every employee who has completed 240 days in 6 days working and 190 days in 5 days working but has not completed the entire year should be considered eligible for gratuity."Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Man sold house but did not file ITR and on getting tax notice he claimed Rs 49 lakh exemption, but taxman denied it; ITAT Mumbai gives relief saying missing original tax return alone cannot shut the door on Section 54
articles.summary: Can you claim an exemption in your income tax return if you have not filed it originally and only initiate ITR filing after getting a notice from the
articles.body: Can you claim an exemption in your income tax return if you have not filed it originally and only initiate ITR filing after getting a notice from the Income Tax Department?In a relief for taxpayers, the Mumbai bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) has ruled that an exemption claim under Section 54 of the Income Tax (I-T) Act for reinvestment of capital gains in a new house cannot be rejected merely because the taxpayer did not initially file an income tax return.The tribunal held that such a claim can be considered and allowed when it is made during reassessment proceedings.What the case is aboutThe case concerned an individual taxpayer who had not submitted an original income tax return under Section 139(1).The dispute concerned the assessment year 2017-18. According to the tribunal's order, the Income Tax Department had information that the man purchased an immovable property valued at Rs 45 lakh during the relevant year. Since he had not filed his income tax return, proceedings were initiated under Section 147 of the Income Tax Act. A notice under Section 148 was issued on March 24, 2024.The man filed his return in response to the notice on April 4, 2024. In it, he claimed an exemption under Section 54 on the capital gains from the sale of a residential property. The sale agreement was dated.In his ITR, the man reported long-term capital gains from the sale of a residential property and sought an exemption of Rs 49 lakh under Section 54, citing his investment in another residential property.Section 54 of the Act allows individuals to claim an exemption on long-term capital gains arising from the sale of a residential property to the extent that the gains are reinvested in purchasing another residential house within the stipulated period.The assessing officer turned down the assessee’s claim, citing the absence of an original income tax return.The assessment order referred to Section 54D while disallowing the claim made under Section 54, and added Rs 31,38,256 to his income.The man challenged the addition before the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals), but the appellate authority upheld the decision. It relied on the Supreme Court's judgment in CIT vs Sun Engineering Works (P.) Ltd., which addresses the limits on claims that can be raised during reassessment proceedings.Why ITAT Mumbai ruled in assessee’s favourITAT Mumbai clarified that although reassessment proceedings cannot be used to reopen matters unrelated to income that has escaped assessment, taxpayers can raise claims that have a direct connection with such income.The ITAT observed that the capital gains in this case were themselves the income that had escaped assessment, making the claim for exemption under Section 54 directly relevant to the calculation of that income.The order explains that the escaped income in this case was the long-term capital gain from the sale of a residential property. The Section 54 claim related to the computation of that very income and was not an unrelated claim raised during reassessment.It therefore held that the exemption request could not be classified as a new or unrelated claim that was impermissible during reassessment proceedings.The tribunal also cited earlier judicial rulings which established that Section 54 does not make filing an income tax return by the prescribed due date a mandatory condition for claiming the exemption. It stressed that a claim submitted in a return filed in response to a reassessment notice cannot be turned down simply because it was made late or the taxpayer had not filed an original return.The order also records that, in a case involving the man’s wife, the assessing officer had accepted a Section 54 deduction claimed in a return filed in response to a reassessment notice for the remaining 50% share of the investment in the new property. The tribunal noted this circumstance while considering the man’s argument.In its reasoning, the tribunal stated that the earlier decisions supported allowing the claim to be examined rather than rejecting it solely because no original return had been filed. It concluded: “We thus, respectfully relying on the above judgments are inclined to allow the appeal of the Assessee, therefore, remand the case to the file of the AO for decision afresh on the claim of the Assessee under section 54 of the Act within the parameters and/or conditions set out in section 54 of the Act but not otherwise.”The ITAT consequently overturned the orders passed by the lower authorities and sent the case back to the assessing officer for fresh consideration.It directed the officer to assess the taxpayer’s entitlement to the Section 54 exemption on merits and grant the benefit if the applicable statutory requirements are met.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Rising tech outages put digital resilience in focus
articles.summary: Tech outages hit Microsoft, AWS, Cloudflare and Apple, disrupting airlines and businesses; experts urge stronger digital resilience and redundancy over breach focus.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Another day, another major technology outage. Over the past week, disruptions have hit Microsoft Outlook and Teams, Cloudflare, AWS, Anthropic’s Claude, Workday, Apple services, the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), United Airlines, JPMorgan Chase and even the US National Security Agency’s classified network, NSANet.In India, a Microsoft cloud outage disrupted email-based customer support at IndiGo, Air India and Akasa Air, while financial services, telecom and IT companies reported problems accessing corporate email and workplace applications. Flight operations were unaffected. Cloudflare also reported disruptions at multiple Indian locations earlier this month.Apple blamed Tuesday’s outages on an internal update, ruling out a cyberattack. The disruptions affected the App Store, iCloud sign-in, Mail and web apps, with some services down for over four hours. While consumer services were restored by Wednesday, two outages affecting its developer platform, App Store Connect, remained listed.“The most alarming thing about this wave of outages is how a failure in one part of our digital infrastructure can disrupt airlines, banks, governments, and millions of people almost simultaneously,” said Tal Kollender, founder and CEO of Israeli cybersecurity firm Remedio.A single misconfiguration, failed update or broken dependency can trigger widespread disruption, she said. As AI becomes embedded in critical infrastructure, autonomous systems making decisions and changes at speeds humans cannot always control could add to the risks. Cybersecurity must move beyond detecting problems to fixing vulnerabilities, with safeguards to ensure corrective actions do not cause further outages, she added.Diwakar Dayal, managing director and area vice-president, SentinelOne India and SAARC, said the biggest cyber risk was not just a breach but the inability to operate when technology failed.“Digital resilience is becoming a new measure of business leadership. In an interconnected world, a technology failure anywhere can become a business crisis everywhere,” he said. For India, where digital infrastructure underpins banking, aviation, public services and commerce, resilience was an economic and national security imperative. Companies need operational redundancy and the ability to contain disruption and recover quickly, he added.Rahul Sasi, CEO and co-founder of CloudSEK, said even unsuccessful cyber exploitation attempts could disrupt services. “Hackers don’t always need to succeed in breaking into a system to cause damage. Sometimes, even a failed attempt can crash an application or bring down an entire service,” he said, citing PHP2Shell. Some publicly available proof-of-concept exploits could crash servers rather than achieve remote code execution, he said. This, however, does not establish that recent outages were caused by cyberattacks.Rajnish Gupta, managing director and country manager, Tenable India, said there was no evidence that AI-driven attacks caused the Microsoft and Cloudflare outages. However, organisations must assess risks across interconnected systems and third-party platforms.Tenable research found that organisations face an average of three attack paths for every security finding.“Cybersecurity is no longer just about preventing attacks. It is about ensuring businesses can survive them,” Dayal said.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.title: Costco sees surge in panic buying after tech outages, report says
articles.summary: Costco shoppers are stocking up on emergency items following a string of tech snafus, according to a Wall Street analyst.
articles.body:
Consumers are panic-buying at Costco, snapping up generators and other emergency-preparedness items in response to a recent string of technology outages , according to investment firm Mizuho Securities.

"Consumer anxiety following the Microsoft Outlook outage, the ground stoppage for all U.S. airline flights, and apocalyptic concerns flaring up across social media have all contributed to increased emergency prep sales at Costco," Mizuho analyst David Bellinger wrote in a report.

Shoppers are "pantry-loading," while 21 of the retailer's 26 "high-ticket generators" were sold out online as of Sunday night, he added.

The recent outages, which blocked access to Microsoft apps , snarled flights nationwide and hindered banking activities at various times during the past week, are raising questions among Americans about a larger cybersecurity threat, CBS News chief correspondent Matt Gutman said on "CBS Mornings" on Wednesday.

The companies affected by the outages have said they were due to issues such as routine maintenance or upgrades, while the Federal Aviation Administration blamed its nationwide ground stop last week on a contractor updating its flight system.

"All of them have denied that cyberattacks are to blame," Gutman said. "Still, the system failures are fueling online speculation about a larger cyber threat."

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Wednesday that there's "zero evidence" that the recent outages in the U.S. are linked.

"The Microsoft incident has nothing to do with what we saw with the FAA . The FAA has nothing to do with what we saw with the banks a few days ago. These issues that we've seen from a technical standpoint are completely unrelated one from another," Rubio said during a news conference in the Philippines.

Costco didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

The close timing of the outages highlights the country's increasing reliance on technology, John D'Arcy, a Temple University professor who researches cybersecurity and information technology failures, told CBS News Philadelphia.

"Our systems are so much more complex and so much more interconnected than they ever have been in the past, that when we just have one failure, the effects are much more dramatic," D'Arcy said.

The surge in panic buying could lift Costco's sales, Bellinger wrote. He raised his target price for the company's stock to $1,150 from $1,100. Other big-box stores, including Walmart and Sam's Club, could see similar "pantry-loading lifts," he added.

Higher borrowing costs could weigh on economic growth and slow the expansion in oil demand. articles.title: 'Are we undervalued?': Uday Kotak asks as Anthropic's valuation tops India's top 10 combined
articles.summary: Anthropic, an AI firm founded just five years ago, is now worth more than India's 10 biggest companies combined. So, is India Inc undervalued?
articles.body: Anthropic, an AI firm founded just five years ago, is now worth more than India's 10 biggest companies combined. So, is India Inc undervalued?Uday Kotak, founder and director of Kotak Mahindra Bank, raised this question while drawing attention to the striking difference between the valuations of global artificial intelligence (AI) businesses and India's largest companies.In a post on X, Kotak pointed to Anthropic, the US-based company behind the Claude AI chatbot, whose valuation has reached $1.5 trillion.“Anthropic, an AI company known for Claude, listed at a valuation of $ 1.5 trillion. It did not exist till ~ 5 years ago. This is more than the combined market cap of the top 10 Indian companies,” Kotak said.He also questioned whether Indian companies were undervalued or needed to adapt to the changing global business landscape.“Are we undervalued, or do we need to catch up in the new world? Or both?” he asked.Anthropic sets IPO price above expected rangeThe offering comprises 980 million shares, according to the company's announcement. articles.title: PANW Stock Surges 8% Overnight: Palo Alto Networks CEO Sees ‘Hundreds Of Billions Of Dollars’ Opportunity In Open-Weight AI Models Security
articles.summary: Palo Alto Networks plans to expand AI security capabilities, building over 100 megawatts of computing capacity through fiscal 2030.
articles.body:
CEO Nikesh Arora said open-weight AI models' share of token usage has climbed from below 5% to over 60% in a year.

Palo Alto Networks has bought Applied Compute for $4.5 billion to strengthen its AI security business.

The company plans to develop over 35 AI-powered security applications and deliver sovereign open-weight models.

Palo Alto Networks (PANW) stock jumped 8% overnight after a third-quarter (Q3) earnings beat, as CEO Nikesh Arora highlighted a market worth billions for securing open-weight AI models. Speaking on the Q3 earnings call, Arora outlined the company's Applied Compute acquisition, which aims to expand enterprise AI security and bring in $1 billion in annual recurring revenue by fiscal 2029.

Palo Alto Networks' stock is on track for a second straight weekly gain.

PANW CEO Sees Open Weight AI Models Gaining Enterprise Interest

Arora said during the Q3 earnings call that businesses are opting for AI models that give them greater ownership and control over their technology. Open-weight models have gained traction, making up more than 60% of token usage, compared with less than 5% a year earlier.

"When organizations put AI at the center of their operations, they want to retain control of their proprietary data, institutional judgment and competitive edge inside their own 4 walls. We expect a future with a serving opportunity in the hundreds of billions of dollars when enterprise applications are driven by open weight and open source adoption."

Applied Compute To Support Palo Alto Networks' AI Security Expansion

To address the enormous security opportunity, Arora said Palo Alto Networks examined potential partners across the AI industry before selecting Applied Compute, citing its engineering capabilities and experience in developing open-weight models through post-training. Palo Alto Networks agreed to acquire Applied Compute in an all-stock deal valued at $4.5 billion.

The Palo Alto-Applied Compute deal will focus on two things. Networks plans to integrate AI into its existing cybersecurity products, developing more than 35 specialized applications that will help customers counter AI-led threats with AI-driven defenses.

The second focus will be developing and delivering secure, sovereign versions of open-weight models for enterprise customers. "To support our efforts, we plan to build out a diversified global influence capability of north of 100-plus megawatts over the next 3 to 5 years," Arora said.

articles.title: ‘Too early’ to determine impact of US blockade on Iran, with Tehran defiant
articles.summary: The US blockade of Iranian ports has a crippling effect on the economy, but Tehran insists its economy can survive.
articles.body:
Tehran, Iran – Iran’s economy is expected to contract further due to the ongoing blockade of its ports by the United States, inflicting pain on tens of millions of Iranians. But experts say it is too early to tell whether Washington’s economic embargo on Tehran is having the desired outcome of either collapsing the Iranian government or forcing it to concede to US demands.

The US believes its naval blockade on Iran, overland trade disruptions and sanctions – part of its maximum pressure campaign on Tehran – are working. The US has also brought a third aircraft carrier into the region to support a potential military escalation, in what appears to be an attempt to force Tehran to capitulate further to its demands.

After a deadlock in the US-Israel war on Iran, which began with strikes that killed Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei on February 28, Washington has demanded Tehran reopen the Strait of Hormuz and curb its nuclear programme.

However, Iranian authorities insist they can withstand the economic pressure and have put forward their demands . Strikes on US interests in the region this week, including radar systems in Bahrain , have been viewed as a defiant response to the US military and economic pressure. But there are signs that the country’s economy and common Iranians are suffering from the current conditions.

Tehran-based economist Peyman Molavi said if current conditions persist, Iran’s inflation could rise considerably over the coming months.

“This will impact parallel markets like foreign currencies, gold, the stock market and housing,” he told Al Jazeera. “But it will unfortunately have the largest impact on the commodities market, from energy to agricultural products, metals, and industrial products.”

For decades, Iran’s governments have increasingly plugged their budget deficits by printing more money, which has saddled the country with a growing money supply, feeding chronic inflation. The foreign currency crunch from disrupted oil exports due to the US military blockade has only exacerbated the situation.

Molavi estimates that the year-on-year growth of the money supply in Iran could rise to 55-60 percent from its current figure of nearly 51 percent by the end of the Persian year in late March. Paired with negative economic growth, he said annual inflation could grow to about 85 percent, and point-to-point inflation to 100 percent.

Iranian Central Bank Governor Abdolnaser Hemmati hit back at US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who has led Washington’s sanctions regime against Tehran.

“Like I said, he must still count his chickens at the end of autumn before moving to winter,” he said in reference to an Iranian proverb – “It’s too early to talk about winter”.

Bessent has claimed the economic embargo will result in a 25 percent contraction of the Iranian economy by the year ending March 2027. Iran’s official figures indicated that the country’s gross domestic product (GDP) shrank by 10.1 percent year-on-year between March 21 and June 20, the first quarter of the Persian calendar year.

Hemmati said the central bank has secured $30bn in foreign currencies to weather the pressure over the coming months, prioritising procurement of essential goods for its citizens.

“American officials believe they can achieve their goals through threats and raise something new each time; from the possibility of collapse to military threats and intensified economic pressure,” Economy Minister Ali Madanizadeh said on Sunday.

All overland routes to and from Iran, except for one with Iraq that was closed due to security reasons, remain open despite the US efforts to isolate Iran from its neighbours, Madanizadeh insisted.

For the seventh Iranian month of Mehr that ended on October 22, the 12-month average annual inflation was at 76.8 percent, according to the Statistical Centre of Iran. Point-to-point inflation, which compares just that month with the same month of the previous year, was at 88.7 percent.

Essential goods have already been experiencing triple-digit inflation for months , with the category of food, beverages and tobacco experiencing year-on-year inflation of 113.4 percent in October, the centre said.

Iranian social media is increasingly filled with personal stories of how most people in the country of about 90 million are rapidly losing their purchasing power.

“Everywhere you look, you could have bought the same commodity with one-fifth of the money last year,” one user wrote on X. “That’s no joke, millions of people have been crushed in between.”

Saleh, a 37-year-old shopkeeper at Tehran’s Grand Bazaar who deals in electric motors for small industrial units, said both domestic and Chinese-made goods can still readily be found in the market. But supply and demand have decreased since US sanctions began to bite.

“The reason is that commodities are expensive, and there’s been a stagnation in the market and also uncertainty over what will happen next,” he told Al Jazeera, asking not to use his full name due to security reasons.

“Everyone’s looking at the dollar price, and manufacturers and clients are making their decisions based on price changes. If we sold 10 items before, now we’re selling three or four, but the price increase maintained some profit. I don’t see the market being near collapse, but there’s less business.”

Companies with an established client base are proving more resilient, he added.

Bessent hailed what is happening in Iran as “one of the fastest collapses in history”, and described the Trump-directed sanctions campaign against Iran as “the greatest economic isolation in the history of the world against a single country”.

He also compared the situation in Iran with the period preceding the fall of the Soviet Union in 1991, saying the country’s economy had shrunk 22 percent over three years before the union collapsed.

Economist Molavi said the comparison may not necessarily translate into immediate economic collapse for Iran as they have fundamentally different economic models .

But he pointed out that Iran’s nominal GDP has fallen from $645bn in 2012 to about $300bn now and that it could decline further if the sanctions continue.

“With the current [level] of underinvestment, halted oil sales, disrupted exports and the sense of suspension in the economy, our economic growth will become even more negative,” he said.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto VI draws rave reviews as gamers enter Vice City
articles.summary: By Aditya Soni and Cordelia Hsu SYDNEY, Nov 19 (Reuters) - After 13 years and an estimated $1 billion or more in production costs, "Grand Theft Auto VI" roll...
articles.body:
SYDNEY, Nov 19 (Reuters) - After 13 years and an estimated $1 billion or more in production costs, "Grand Theft Auto VI" rolled out across the globe on Thursday, gaining rapturous early reviews for the most anticipated video game release in history.

The game, which could bring in billions of dollars for its developer, Take-Two Interactive studio Rockstar Games, raced to the top of Metacritic's all-time gaming leaderboard with a score ‌of 99, a mark matched by only one other title, Nintendo's 1998 classic "The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time".

The game went online as midnight struck in New Zealand on Thursday, with launches following the clock worldwide, spurring parties, ‌posts from world leaders, and some companies giving employees the day off to play it.

"It is the best game that's ever been made and we're only 20 minutes deep," said 33-year-old Asif Mir as he started to play and livestream just after midnight in Sydney, one of the first places where the game ​was unlocked.

In London, gamers counted down to the release at parties across the city.

"Today has been a day that I have waited for my whole life," said 20-year-old influencer Archie Whitby.

"To be living it, it feels almost dystopian. It doesn't feel real."

Miami, the inspiration for the game's fictional Vice City setting, was one of the last places to get in on the action.

The city's NBA team, the Miami Heat, celebrated the release with a Vice City-themed match against the Milwaukee Bucks, with the court and stadium adorned with the game's colours of neon pink and blue.

Millions of players have already downloaded the game to their consoles, with many taking time off work — or calling in sick — to play the latest installment in a franchise that since its 1997 debut has become one of the best-selling video game series ‌of all time.

"It's the Star Wars of this generation," said Joost van Dreunen, adjunct ⁠professor at NYU Stern School of Business.

"It's a synchronized, shared event. So millions of people will all want to be there the first couple of days, the first few weeks of experiencing it as it goes live."

Strong initial reviews of the game — available on Sony's ( SONY ) PlayStation 5 and Microsoft's ( MSFT ) Xbox Series X and S consoles — helped push up Take-Two Interactive's US shares by 6.5% on Wednesday afternoon in ⁠New York.

'TRULY ASTONISHING': GAME GETS STRONG USER REVIEWS

The original "Grand Theft Auto" looks basic by today's standards, with a storyline — stealing cars and carrying out jobs for crime syndicates — that angered politicians and parents, even as it delighted fans.

articles.title: PFRDA looking at ways to incentivise distribution without reducing returns
articles.summary: MUMBAI: PFRDA is examining ways to improve pension distribution by addressing low distributor commissions, which remain at a fifth of mutual fund industry
articles.body: MUMBAI: PFRDA is examining ways to improve pension distribution by addressing low distributor commissions, which remain at a fifth of mutual fund industry levels despite a 2.5-fold increase. The regulator is also reviewing investment allocation to improve long-term returns, including greater exposure to growth assets and alternative investment funds, PFRDA chairman S Ramann said.Pension distributors receive a fifth of the commissions available to mutual fund distributors despite PFRDA having increased the distributable commission pool 2.5 times. Ramann said low commissions were one of the reasons pension products had failed to gain wider acceptance. "We actually have a bit of an inverse problem as compared to the insurance industry where we have money on the table for the distributors is so abysmally low that it's one of the reasons why probably the pension product never really went out in a big way.So, even after having increased the total sort of distributable commissions that lie on the table two and a half times, we're still one-fifth the commission's level which is available in the mutual fund industry," he said. He was speaking at the Gatekeepers of Governance 2026 event in Mumbai.The regulator is also weighing the need to balance distributor incentives with the cost borne by subscribers over the long term. Ramann said commissions on pension products needed to be assessed over their long investment horizon, which could extend to 30 or 50 years. "Over that period of time, we should probably count the compounding effect of that commission also. And that's really when we start getting into this conflict of what should be a fair commission or a total cost to the customer," he said.The regulator has set up two expert committees to examine asset allocation, one under former SBI chairman Dinesh Khara and another headed by investment expert Narayan Ramachandran, who has worked with mutual funds.Ramann said the committees had provided inputs on whether pension savings were being allocated to the appropriate asset classes to generate returns for retirement payouts. He cited Australia's superannuation programme, the equivalent of India's defined contribution pension system, where 72% of the corpus is invested in growth assets, with around 28% in fixed income. Nearly half of the growth-asset allocation is in unlisted investments.India's pension ecosystem remains risk-averse, with inadequate capital flowing into greenfield projects and startups, Ramann said. NPS has started its own fund of funds to invest in AIFs, allowing pension savings to gain exposure to a diversified pool of investments. "It is citizens' money going into the AIFs, so that they get a respectable and a better sort of diversified return," he said.On pension payouts, PFRDA is examining the possibility of introducing a market-based guarantee mechanism for private-sector subscribers. A committee headed by Sahu is studying the proposal, though Ramann said guarantees would involve costs. "Our job is to look at it, look at the future, see what we can build in baby steps maybe," he said.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.title: Dollar eases after seven-session rally, rates and equities in focus
articles.summary: By Stefano Rebaudo Nov 19 (Reuters) - The US dollar index edged down on Thursday after a seven-session winning streak but remained underpinned by hawkish rem...
articles.body:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - The US dollar index edged down on Thursday after a seven-session winning streak but remained underpinned by hawkish remarks from a Federal Reserve official that reinforced the case for further rate hikes.

Fed ‌Governor Christopher Waller called for a more aggressive response to inflation, while minutes of the central bank's October 27 ‌to 28 meeting showed policymakers increasingly concerned that additional tightening might be needed.

The dollar rally started on November 10 when hotter-than-expected US inflation data bolstered expectations ​that the Fed would raise borrowing costs next month.

The dollar index this week reached its highest level since April 2, 2025, when US President Donald Trump revealed a sweeping tariff package, triggering a selloff in US assets.

It was last down 0.05% at 103.73, after reaching 103.97.

Barclays analysts said fiscal stimulus and strong AI-related capital spending point to a resilient US economy, a wider output gap and higher-for-longer interest rates, ‌all supportive of dollar strength.

The dollar's gains have ⁠come despite a selloff in technology shares.

"First, the market has also repriced a more hawkish Fed given recent commentary pushing the interest rate differential wider, but the dollar seems to be overshooting this move," ⁠said George Saravelos, global head of forex strategy at Deutsche Bank, explaining the recent rise.

"Second, and more intriguingly, foreigners have been very aggressive buyers of US equities even as the stock market has tumbled," he added.

A Deutsche Bank tracker following more than 100 foreign-domiciled exchange-traded funds showed ​large ​dip-buying of US stocks by foreigners over the last two weeks, the ​biggest buying spree so far this year.

Such a move ‌reinforces the view that the dollar has been supported by investor flows into US equities.

Shares in Nvidia fell overnight even after the chip bellwether beat revenue and guidance forecasts, amid uncertainty caused by co-founder Jensen Huang's sudden departure as CEO last week following his admission of extramarital affairs.

The dollar was up 0.25% to 159.75 yen, snapping a four-day losing streak.

Analysts said that a further selloff in AI-linked assets could support the yen through safe-haven buying and repatriation flows, with the impact likely to be ‌more pronounced against other currencies than against the dollar.

According to Barclays estimates, ​a 10% decline in the S&P 500 from its peak could push dollar/yen ​towards 155, while a 20% decline could pressure it ​towards 152.

articles.title: Bengaluru–Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper is the fastest train on the route and cuts travel time by nearly 6 hours to 16 hours 10 minutes, but its AC 3 fare of Rs 2,810 is 60–96% higher than rival trains
articles.summary: Indian Railways has started the rollout of Vande Bharat sleepers with the new trains being rolled out on three key routes on its network so far.
articles.body: Indian Railways has started the rollout of Vande Bharat sleepers with the new trains being rolled out on three key routes on its network so far.The Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper, was recently inaugurated by Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw. It is the fastest train on the route, offering passengers modern facilities.After the train was flagged off, the Railway Ministry described the new Vande Bharat Sleeper Express as an important addition to overnight rail connectivity between the two metropolitan cities."The new service will offer passengers an additional convenient travel option, enabling them to undertake long-distance journeys overnight and reach their destination the following day," the Ministry stated.The service will stop at several key stations on the route, including Anantapur, Guntakal, Raichur, Yadgir, Wadi, Kalaburagi, Solapur, Pune and Kalyan.Fastest train on Mumbai-Bengaluru routeCommercial services from Mumbai began on November 2, and the train has already attracted strong demand. All classes are fully booked, with passengers being waitlisted for the next couple of weeks.Railway officials said existing trains generally take around 22 hours or longer to cover the distance of more than 1,100 km between Bengaluru and Mumbai. The Vande Bharat Sleeper completes the journey in 16 hours and 10 minutes, making it the fastest service on the route and cutting travel time by nearly six hours.The train leaves Sir M. Visvesvaraya Terminal Bengaluru (SMVT Bengaluru) at 1945 hours and arrives at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT), Mumbai, at 1155 hours the following day. On the return journey, it departs from CSMT at 2010 hours and reaches SMVT Bengaluru at 1200 hours the next day.The service runs six days a week. Trains departing from Bengaluru do not operate on Mondays, while departures from Mumbai are suspended on Tuesdays.According to officials, approximately 22 trains run between Mumbai and Bengaluru, including services connecting stations in the vicinity of the two cities.According to the Ministry, the new train will improve rail connectivity across parts of Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra, making important commercial, educational and regional centres more accessible.Vande Bharat sleeper fares on Mumbai-BengaluruHowever, according to a PTI report, the speed and amenities come at a considerably higher cost than travel on other trains connecting the two cities.Passengers travelling in AC 3 Tier pay 60–96% more than the fares charged by other trains on the route.The premium is also substantial in the higher classes, with AC 2 Tier tickets costing 65–78% more and AC 1 Tier fares being 20–30% higher than those for comparable coaches on existing services, according to a PTI analysis.A ticket on the Vande Bharat Sleeper costs Rs 2,810 for AC 3 Tier, Rs 3,630 for AC 2 Tier and Rs 4,450 for AC 1 Tier for the Bengaluru-Mumbai journey.Among the other relatively fast services on this route is the Coimbatore-Mumbai LTT Express (Train No. 11014), which takes about 21 hours and 55 minutes to travel from Bengaluru to Mumbai. Its fares stand at Rs 1,435 for AC 3 Tier, Rs 2,045 for AC 2 Tier and Rs 3,425 for AC 1 Tier.The Ajmer Express also covers a comparable distance in approximately 22 hours. Passengers pay Rs 1,510 for AC 3 Tier, Rs 2,155 for AC 2 Tier and Rs 3,610 for AC 1 Tier on this train.Vande Bharat Sleeper fares are also higher when compared with the premium Humsafar Express. Its AC 3 Tier fare is nearly 63% higher, at Rs 2,810 against Rs 1,725 on the Humsafar Express.Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw has defended the higher fares charged by different train services in Parliament, explaining that ticket prices reflect the amenities available onboard and that Indian Railways operates services tailored to different categories of passengers."The fares of various trains/classes are based on the facilities provided in these trains. Indian Railways (IR) run various types of train services for different types of passenger segments. Evaluation and rationalization of passenger fares, including those of Vande Bharat trains, is a continuous and on-going process," Vaishnaw had said in the Lok Sabha in March 2025.Vande Bharat sleeper featuresThe train is capable of reaching speeds of up to 180 kmph and has received clearance to operate at 160 kmph. However, the maximum speed permitted on a particular route will depend on the clearance granted for individual sections.Passenger comfort has been factored into the train's design, which includes ergonomically designed, odour-free toilets equipped with vacuum evacuation systems. Dedicated berths and toilet facilities have also been provided for differently-abled passengers.To make long-distance travel more convenient, the train offers modern onboard amenities and ample space for storing luggage. Its integrated BRL units are equipped with a three-pin charging socket and switch, while Type A and Type C USB ports provide additional options for charging electronic devices.The train's engineering incorporates regenerative braking technology to enhance energy efficiency, alongside an under-slung propulsion system. Its advanced aerodynamic design is intended to enable smoother acceleration and minimise jerks during the journey.The coaches feature a car body made of austenitic stainless steel, designed to comply with EN15227 crash standards. A fully sealed, flexible gangway with a quick-release mechanism is another feature. Centrally controlled, single-leaf automatic sliding plug doors provide access between the train and its surroundings.Measures to insulate and reduce noise have been incorporated to create a quieter environment inside the passenger saloons. The interiors are also equipped with direct and indirect LED lighting and sensor-based intercommunication doors.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.summary: In a big move that will benefit lakhs of provident fund subscribers, the Central Board of Trustees (CBT) has approved a proposal to introduce a Systematic
articles.body: In a big move that will benefit lakhs of provident fund subscribers, the Central Board of Trustees (CBT) has approved a proposal to introduce a Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) for retiring members of the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO).The Times of India had first reported about the proposal being under consideration today. Under the proposed facility, members will be able to receive their accumulated provident fund savings in instalments over a period of time instead of taking out the entire amount at once.What is EPFO’s SWP for your PF account?The SWP is intended to help members turn their retirement savings into a regular and predictable source of income while retaining ownership of the underlying corpus, according to an ANI report quoting EPFO.At present, members are required to withdraw their entire provident fund corpus within three years of retirement to avoid their accounts becoming inoperative and ceasing to earn annual interest.If a member dies while receiving payments, the nominee or dependent will have the option of withdrawing the remaining balance or continuing to receive periodic payouts.According to the EPFO, the initiative will strengthen financial security after retirement by offering a flexible and dependable income stream while protecting the interests of members’ families.The plan would give crores of existing subscribers access to the facility as well, particularly those who find it difficult to manage their retirement savings prudently.The proposal was discussed at a meeting of the central board of trustees on Thursday, chaired by Labour Minister Mansukh Mandaviya.According to the TOI report, in its initial phase, the voluntary scheme is expected to focus on existing EPFO subscribers. The organisation estimates that around 6.3 lakh members aged above 55 years could benefit from the facility at the outset.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.title: Household savings must go not just to equity but all parts of life-cycle capital : Dipam Secretary
articles.summary: MUMBAI: DIPAM (Department of Investment and Public Asset Management) secretary Arunish Chawla has called for a restructuring of India's financing
articles.body: MUMBAI: DIPAM (Department of Investment and Public Asset Management) secretary Arunish Chawla has called for a restructuring of India's financing ecosystem to channel household savings into a wider range of assets, mobilise pension and insurance funds for long-term investment, deepen fixed-income markets and expand domestic participation in alternative investment funds. He has argued that policy, tax and regulatory frameworks need to evolve to direct capital towards the financing requirements of Viksit Bharat.Addressing the CII DFS Financing Summit 2026, he said household savings had traditionally been concentrated in real estate, gold and valuables rather than financial assets. Changing this pattern would require policy, regulatory and tax incentives to bring more household savings into the formal financial system. "The question is how we can incentivize a behavioral change through policy, through regulation, through tax incentives, in a way that ordinary Indians, working Indians, saving Indians become part of our formalized financial economy and help enhance growth and also finance the financing needs of a Viksit Bharat in both public and private sectors," he said.He said the expansion of demat accounts and mutual fund assets showed the growing participation of households in capital markets. Demat accounts had increased from around 3.6 crore in 2019 to 25 crore in Oct 2026, while mutual fund assets under management had risen from Rs 15 lakh crore in 2016 to Rs 84 lakh crore.However, he said financialisation of household savings needed to extend beyond equity markets to finance companies at different stages of their life cycle. "Household savings... can be channeled and recycled to not just our equity markets, but all parts of our life-cycle capital," he said.Another challenge was the imbalance between equity and fixed-income markets. While India's market capitalisation ranked among the four or five largest globally, the development of bond markets remained important to provide companies with alternatives to equity financing. "How we develop the bond side, the fixed-income side of our markets, and how we incentivize it vis-à-vis equity is going to be another very big challenge into the next 20 years," he said.He also called for a greater role for market-based financing in meeting long-term investment requirements, arguing that banks, given the structure of their deposits and lending, were primarily suited to medium-term financing. Pension and insurance funds, whose assets were growing, could provide a source of long-term capital.The DIPAM secretary also called for expanding domestic participation in alternative investment funds (AIFs), including venture capital and private equity. He said the AIF industry, with cumulative investments of Rs 7.5 lakh crore, was around one-tenth the size of the mutual fund industry, whose cumulative investments stood at Rs 84 lakh crore.Money habits form by age 7.
