articles.title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq futures rise ahead of historic Anthropic IPO
articles.summary: Anthropic's public trading debut under the ticker symbol ANT marks a pivotal moment for the artificial intelligence boom.
articles.body: US stock futures rose on Thursday as investors awaited Anthropic's (ANT) public trading debut, which marks a pivotal moment for the artificial intelligence boom.Futures on the Dow Jones Industrial Average (YM=F) rose 0.6%, while those on the S&P 500 (ES=F) added 1%. Contracts for the Nasdaq-100 (NQ=F) advanced 2% as tech stocks tentatively rose in premarket trading.All eyes were on Anthropic after the Claude maker priced its initial public offering (IPO) at $83 per share and expanded its offering to 925 million shares due to strong investor demand. At that price, Anthropic is valued at over $1 trillion, less than the market cap of SpaceX (SPCX) when it went public in June, but still larger than Walmart (WMT), Micron (MU), and AMD (AMD). Follow live updates on Anthropic and its public debut as ANT begins tradingThe timing of Anthropic's IPO coincides with a period of upheaval for the AI trade amid anxieties over safety, the durability of the boom, and an incoming Democratic-led Congress. The market's response to Anthropic's debut could set the tone for other companies eyeing the public markets, notably OpenAI (OPAI.PVT) — which, according to CEO Sam Altman, still plans to go public.While Anthropic's IPO will be the main course, we'll also be paying attention to several other happenings on Thursday. President Trump is currently in Shenzhen, China, for the APEC Summit, where he met with world leaders, including Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Questions about semiconductor export controls and tariffs are top of mind for Trump's visit.At the same time, consumer bellwether Walmart (WMT) reports earnings before the bell, and other retailers, such as The Gap (GAP) and Bath & Body Works (BBWI), will also report results. Initial jobless claims and manufacturing activity data will provide updates on the US's economic health.We're also watching to see if Nvidia (NVDA) stock can shake off five straight days of losses as uncertainty over the AI chipmaker's leadership overshadowed its solid earnings report on Tuesday.

articles.title: Anthropic's record-breaking IPO: How can Indian investors buy shares in Claude's parent company
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Anthropic has just rewritten the IPO record books, raising $81.31 billion through its stock market offering and surpassing SpaceX's $75 billion
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Anthropic has just rewritten the IPO record books, raising $81.31 billion through its stock market offering and surpassing SpaceX's $75 billion fundraising haul. For investors who have watched the artificial intelligence race unfold from the sidelines, this could look like a chance to finally get a slice of the action.But for Indian investors hoping to own a piece of the company behind AI chatbot Claude, there is a catch: they will have to wait for its US market debut and buy shares at the prevailing market price, rather than the IPO offer price.Anthropic is scheduled to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 19, 2026, under the ticker symbol “ANT”. With the IPO subscription window now closed, resident Indian investors who missed the offering cannot buy shares at the original offer price. Their entry point will instead depend on the stock's market price once trading begins, which could mean paying a premium.The offering has attracted strong interest from investors worldwide, with Anthropic expected to command a valuation of more than $1 trillion. This would place it among the world's most valuable publicly traded technology companies.The IPO comprises 980 million Class A common shares. Of these, Anthropic is offering 956.35 million shares, while certain existing shareholders are selling the remaining 23.65 million. The company has clarified that it will not receive any proceeds from the sale of shares by these existing shareholders.Here's how Indian investors can buy its sharesMissing the IPO subscription window does not necessarily mean missing out on the stock altogether. Once Anthropic begins trading in the US, Indian residents can purchase its shares through overseas brokerage accounts that provide access to Nasdaq-listed stocks.Investors can make these investments through the Reserve Bank of India's Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) route. The process requires them to complete KYC formalities, submit the necessary tax documentation and transfer funds through an authorised banking channel.GIFT City-based investment platforms are another possible route, with some offering access to US equities. However, this depends on their product offerings and regulatory arrangements.Before choosing a platform, investors should check whether it will support trading in Anthropic shares from the listing date. Zerodha, Groww and HDFC Securities are among the stock brokerage platforms that offer access to overseas stocks.How much can Indian investors put into US stocksThe RBI's Liberalised Remittance Scheme allows Indian residents to remit up to $250,000 per financial year for permitted purposes. The limit covers investments in foreign stocks and overseas-listed exchange-traded funds (ETFs), as well as expenses such as travel and education.Importantly, the entire $250,000 allowance can be used for investments in the US stock market, provided the investor does not need to use any part of it for other permitted overseas expenses during that financial year.For instance, if an investor does not plan to send money to children studying abroad or meet other eligible overseas expenses, the full annual remittance limit can be used for investments in US stocks.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Gold was at Rs 1.81 lakh at the start of 2026, and now it has crashed almost 29% to Rs 1.29 lakh per 10 grams; why is gold falling and how much more will it drop?
articles.summary: Gold prices have been tanking in the last few weeks, going way below their lifetime highs seen at the start of this year.
articles.body: Gold prices have been tanking in the last few weeks, going way below their lifetime highs seen at the start of this year. From Rs 1.81 lakh per 10 grams to Rs 1.29 lakh - that’s a fall of almost 29%.Gold futures edged down by Rs 44 to Rs 1,29,770 per 10 grams on Thursday, as demand in the spot market remained subdued.On the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), gold contracts for December delivery slipped Rs 44, or 0.03%, to Rs 1,29,770 per 10 grams. The contracts recorded a trading volume of 12,735 lots.Analysts attributed the marginal fall in gold prices to weak spot demand.In international markets, gold futures were largely unchanged at $3,739.85 per ounce in New York.Why is gold falling?So why is gold falling off the cliff suddenly? We ask experts:Gold’s initial decline followed profit-booking by investors after prices had risen to high levels, setting off a steep correction. Before the metal could stabilise, the US-Iran war erupted, sending crude oil prices past $120 per barrel and heightening fears of rising inflation.More recently, an unusually sharp surge in real yields has added to the pressure on gold prices, prompting further selling. The US Federal Reserve has increased interest rates for the first time since 2023. As inflation continues to remain high, expectations that the central bank could raise rates again in the coming months have gained strength.According to commodity analyst Maneesh Sharma, gold gave breakout below the previous consolidation range for the first time since September 2025 breaching the critical $3,800/Oz levels in Spot as strengthening bets on aggressive Fed tightening, amid rising inflationary concerns, strong consumer spending and hawkish central bank rhetoric, continued to fuel strength in dollar.What needs to be understood is that gold is a non interest yielding asset and when the US central bank hikes rates, bomd yields rise, shifting investor money to them.“The Dollar Index stands at its highest level in over 18 months against its major rivals, while the benchmark 10-year US Treasury bond yields held firm around 5.10%,” he tells TOI.“Expectations of further Fed tightening in the coming months remains a headwind for gold in near term while gold is expected to remain volatile, with the direction of US yields and dollar index likely to remain the key drivers,” he adds.Jateen Trivedi, VP Research Analyst - Commodity and Currency, LKP Securities says gold has witnessed significant profit booking in November month from Rs 1,450,00 to Rs 1,290,00 as market participants increasingly priced in the possibility of a US rate hike in December. Elevated inflation concerns and stronger demand for the dollar as a safe-haven asset have weighed on bullion.“Higher living and consumer spending costs could also limit investment demand for precious metals,” he tells TOI.Netra Deshpande, Research Analyst, Mirae Asset Sharekhan explains that precious metals are trading under pressure in the Indian markets tracking the global sell-off, dollar rise and underlying bullions falling sharply in the international markets on rising expectations of a Fed rate hike in December.“Domestic sentiment is also hurt by expectations that the RBI may raise rates at its December MPC meeting,” she tells TOI.“A sell-off in AI-related stocks has also added some liquidation in the counter to cover losses, but central bank gold purchases reached 321t in Q3, giving some support to the prices. Total SPDR gold ETF holdings are still up 2% this year at 100.9 million oz. Global geopolitical uncertainties also add to the safe haven bid,” she adds.Silver is falling sharply as tightening policies and slower growth weaken industrial demand.Where is gold headed?Analysts have mixed views on the near-term and long-term outlook for gold and silver.According to Maneesh Sharma, the 21-week EMA trading at around $3965/Oz is likely to remain a key upside barrier for Spot gold (CMP 3772/Oz). With no nearby moving-average-based supports on the chart, the metal remains vulnerable to further downside up to $3670 – 3640/Oz zone in near term basis in spot.“With gold yet to witness a new low for year 2026 it is still expected to outperform Silver in near term,” Sharma says“Meanwhile, the current fall in prices of gold has also delayed the expectation of a meaningful recovery in the first half of 2027, a 10–15 % recovery above $4500/Oz still looks possible in the second half of 2027 considering continued central-bank purchase & broader ETF inflows would strengthen support,” he adds.Jateen Trivedi cautions that with the Dollar Index hovering near 103.50, the near-term outlook for gold remains weak.“COMEX Gold needs to reclaim $4,000 to improve sentiment, while sustained trading below this level could keep downside pressure intact, with major support seen near 3,550–3,500,” he says.“For a longer term perspective Rs 1,100,00 remains the support and 1,450,00 as a major resistance now,” Trivedi cautions.According to Netra Deshpande, the major immediate support for gold is around Rs 1,310,00 per 10 gram and for silver around Rs 1,630,00 per kg on MCX.“Overall, gold and silver are likely to trade in the steady to lower but wedding and festive jewellery demand and central bank buying will cap to the further sharp downside. Overall bullish bias in the long run is still intact in the domestic market,” she believes.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. articles.title: Oil prices rise as Middle East shipping attacks counter supply surplus outlook
articles.summary: By Seher Dareen LONDON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Oil prices edged up on Thursday following losses in the prior session as worries about Middle East supplies amid a...
articles.body:
LONDON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Oil prices edged up on Thursday following losses in the prior session as worries about Middle East supplies amid attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz pushed ‌up against expectations for a market surplus.

Brent crude futures were trading up 24 cents, or 0.26%, at $92.19 ‌a barrel at 0953 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate futures for December were up 5 cents to $83.31. The December contract expires on Friday and ​the more active January contract was up 12 cents at $82.43.

While there was still uncertainty around whether oil prices would have another flare-up or break to the downside, it should be noted that Brent has not been able to stay below $90 a barrel, PVM Associates analyst John Evans said.

"There is little chance that any solution to both the Ukraine war and Iran ‌conflict being achieved by the trilateral meeting ⁠in Shenzhen, but in the small chance something comes of it, entering into fresh length in this current environment does not seem altogether attractive," he said.

US President Donald Trump and ⁠his Chinese and Russian counterparts, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, kicked off a three-way meeting, with Trump saying both he and Xi felt strongly about oil having to flow through the Strait of Hormuz.

Still, risks remained for Middle East oil supply amid the ​US-Israeli ​war on Iran.

Iran's navy said three oil tankers sailing east ​of the Strait of Hormuz were disabled by ‌mines, Iranian media reported on Wednesday.

On Thursday, the Iran-aligned Houthi movement fired missiles at the Saudi Arabian capital Riyadh, but the Saudi Civil Defense agency said the danger had passed.

Reuters reported on Wednesday that Ukrainian drone attacks have reduced Russian oil refineries' combined crude processing volumes by 45% since late October, citing industry sources.

"Intensifying Ukrainian attacks on Russian energy infrastructure are keeping supply risks elevated for both crude oil and products, with production and exports falling," analysts at ‌ANZ said in a note.

A larger-than-expected rise in US oil stockpiles ​reported on Wednesday, however, weighed on the market outlook. US crude inventories ​rose by 3.4 million barrels to 417.8 million ​barrels for the week that ended on November 13, the EIA said, compared with analysts' ‌expectations in a Reuters poll for a rise of ​58,000 barrels.

Brent fell 1.3% in ​the previous session, while WTI dropped 3.2% to its lowest point since August 26 on emerging expectations of a supply surplus.

articles.title: Palo Alto Networks CEO just dropped a truth bomb on the network outages sweeping through major companies
articles.summary: Cybersecurity giant keeps real on the alarming number of network outages.
articles.body:
A cybersecurity CEO offers plain talk on the outages sweeping through major companies and disrupting everything from your email to your flight.

"I want to be clear, there are two distinct parallel effects that are driving this environment. The first effect is a massive surge in vulnerabilities and patches being deployed. We're seeing critical and severe vulnerabilities discovered nearly seven times the monthly average of last year. These discoveries are happening at a speed and intensity which is hard for IT teams to cope with," Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ) CEO Nikesh Arora said on his earnings call Wednesday evening.

Added Arora, "We believe many of the major disruptions of the last few weeks, including outages across major enterprises and governments, were partially due to unintended consequences of patching and configuration changes, as IT teams simply cannot patch these vulnerabilities fast enough without compromising their production environments. The second effect is the rise of AI-assisted cyberattacks. Bad actors are using open-weight models and new agentic frameworks to find and exploit vulnerabilities at unprecedented speed and scale. New agentic frameworks like ARTEX are enabling bad actors to turn simple instructions into autonomous, multi-stage attacks, allowing a handful of operators to compromise dozens of targets simultaneously. As we look ahead, we anticipate an elevated threat environment."

Something is breaking across corporate America — and the timing is getting harder to ignore.

United Airlines ( UAL ) suffered a system outage that delayed departing flights. JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ) experienced a software bug that slowed transactions and caused knock-on problems for customers at other banks, including Bank of America ( BAC ).

Just days earlier, an FAA network failure grounded flights nationwide for more than four hours. Microsoft's ( MSFT ) Outlook outage last week disrupted businesses around the world.

These incidents appear unrelated, and there is no evidence of a coordinated cyberattack. But when airlines, banks, and critical government systems all stumble within days of each other, it raises questions about critical infrastructure's vulnerability amid the push to advance AI.

The backdrop continues to be fertile ground for a cybersecurity player like Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ).

Revenue and operating profit for the most recent quarter surged 39% and 47%, respectively, from the year-ago period. Guidance for the current quarter and full year was also ahead of consensus estimates.
